learn.hero: CodeCome audits source code with AI agents, in six steps. Each step leaves files on disk that the next one reads, and a check decides whether it may continue.
learn.s1.click: Phases 4 and 5 run once per finding: that is why they look stacked.
learn.s1.lead: The code goes in on the left and a report comes out on the right. Click a phase to see what it does.
learn.s1.title: The whole picture: six phases
learn.s2.agent_sub: the model of the chosen profile
learn.s2.lead: Every phase is the same machine: instructions, an agent that works in a loop with tools, results written to disk, and a gate.
learn.s2.p1: The agent does not answer in one go: it reads the code, runs commands and writes notes, step by step, until the phase's goal is met.
learn.s2.p2: Everything it learns is saved as plain Markdown/YAML files. There is no hidden database: you can open and review every file.
learn.s2.p3: The gate is a deterministic script, not the AI: it checks that the expected files exist and are well formed before letting the audit move on.
learn.s2.title: Inside a phase
learn.s3.lead: A finding starts as a suspicion and only counts once it has been proven.
learn.s3.p1: Phase 2 writes each suspicion as a PENDING finding, with the file, the line and why it looks vulnerable.
learn.s3.p2: Phase 4 tries to reproduce it for real in an isolated sandbox: if it works it is CONFIRMED, with evidence; if not, REJECTED.
learn.s3.p3: Phase 5 goes one step further and builds a working proof of concept. Only EXPLOITED findings are beyond doubt.
learn.s3.title: The life of a finding
